title: Viking Raid on Lindisfarne
description: Norse raiders attacked the monastery of Lindisfarne in England, an event traditionally marking the start of the Viking Age.

title: Unification under Harald Fairhair
description: Harald Fairhair won the Battle of Hafrsfjord, traditionally credited with unifying Norway into a single kingdom.

title: Christianization of Norway
description: Around the turn of the millennium, kings such as Olav Tryggvason and later Olav Haraldsson promoted the conversion of Norway to Christianity.

title: Kalmar Union Formed
description: Norway joined Denmark and Sweden under a single monarch in the Kalmar Union, beginning centuries of union with neighbors.

title: Norwegian Constitution Signed
description: Norway adopted its constitution at Eidsvoll on 17 May, asserting independence before entering a union with Sweden.

title: Independence from Sweden
description: Norway peacefully dissolved its union with Sweden and became a fully sovereign kingdom under Haakon VII.

title: North Sea Oil Discovered
description: The Ekofisk field discovery launched Norway's petroleum industry, transforming it into one of the world's wealthiest nations.

title: Baptism of Mieszko I
description: Duke Mieszko I adopted Christianity, an event regarded as the founding moment of the Polish state.

title: Coronation of Bolesław I
description: Bolesław I the Brave was crowned the first King of Poland, elevating the duchy to a kingdom.

title: Battle of Grunwald
description: Polish-Lithuanian forces decisively defeated the Teutonic Knights, one of the largest battles of medieval Europe.

title: Union of Lublin
description: Poland and Lithuania formed the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, creating one of Europe's largest states.

title: Third Partition of Poland
description: Russia, Prussia, and Austria completed the partitions, erasing Poland from the map for 123 years.

title: Poland Regains Independence
description: After World War I, Poland was reconstituted as a sovereign republic, ending over a century of partition.

title: Solidarity Movement Founded
description: The Solidarity trade union emerged at the Gdańsk shipyard, becoming a key force against communist rule.

title: Poland Joins the European Union
description: Poland became a member of the European Union, deepening its integration with Western Europe.

title: Kingdom of Portugal Founded
description: Afonso Henriques proclaimed himself King of Portugal after victory at the Battle of Ourique, establishing the kingdom.

title: Treaty of Zamora
description: The Kingdom of León recognized Portuguese independence under Afonso Henriques in the Treaty of Zamora.

title: Capture of Ceuta
description: Portugal seized the North African city of Ceuta, marking the beginning of the Portuguese Age of Discovery.

title: Vasco da Gama Reaches India
description: Vasco da Gama completed the first sea voyage from Europe to India, opening a maritime trade route.

title: Great Lisbon Earthquake
description: A devastating earthquake and tsunami destroyed much of Lisbon, profoundly affecting Portugal and Enlightenment thought.

title: Proclamation of the Republic
description: A revolution overthrew the monarchy and established the Portuguese First Republic.

title: Carnation Revolution
description: A largely peaceful military coup ended the Estado Novo dictatorship and restored democracy to Portugal.

title: Portugal Joins the EEC
description: Portugal became a member of the European Economic Community, integrating with the broader European market.

title: Dacian Kingdom under Burebista
description: Burebista unified the Dacian tribes into a powerful kingdom in the region of modern Romania.

title: Roman Conquest of Dacia
description: Emperor Trajan defeated the Dacians, making Dacia a Roman province and shaping Romania's Latin heritage.

title: Union under Michael the Brave
description: Michael the Brave briefly united Wallachia, Moldavia, and Transylvania, an enduring symbol of Romanian unity.

title: Union of the Principalities
description: Wallachia and Moldavia united under Alexandru Ioan Cuza, forming the basis of modern Romania.

title: Romania Declares Independence
description: Romania declared independence from the Ottoman Empire, internationally recognized after the Russo-Turkish War.

title: Great Union of Transylvania
description: Transylvania, Bessarabia, and Bukovina united with the Kingdom of Romania, forming Greater Romania.

title: Romanian Revolution
description: A popular uprising overthrew the communist regime of Nicolae Ceaușescu, ending decades of dictatorship.

title: Romania Joins the European Union
description: Romania became a full member of the European Union, advancing its post-communist integration with Europe.

title: Founding of Kievan Rus
description: Oleg of Novgorod established Kiev as the capital, forming the medieval state of Kievan Rus.

title: Christianization of Rus
description: Vladimir the Great adopted Orthodox Christianity, shaping the religious and cultural identity of the East Slavs.

title: Ivan IV Crowned Tsar
description: Ivan the Terrible became the first crowned Tsar of all Russia, centralizing power in Moscow.

title: Founding of Saint Petersburg
description: Peter the Great founded Saint Petersburg as a new capital, opening Russia toward Europe.

title: Napoleon's Invasion Repelled
description: Russia withstood Napoleon's invasion, whose Grande Armée was destroyed during the retreat from Moscow.

title: Russian Revolution
description: The Bolshevik Revolution overthrew the provisional government, leading to the creation of the Soviet state.

title: First Human in Space
description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first person to orbit the Earth aboard Vostok 1.

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
description: The USSR collapsed and the Russian Federation emerged as an independent sovereign state.

title: Traditional Founding of San Marino
description: According to tradition, the stonemason Saint Marinus founded a community on Monte Titano, the basis of the republic.

title: First Captains Regent
description: San Marino established the office of the Captains Regent, the foundation of its enduring republican government.

title: Statutes of San Marino Adopted
description: San Marino codified its constitutional statutes, among the oldest written governing documents still in use.

title: Independence Recognized by Papacy
description: The Papacy formally recognized San Marino's independence, securing the small republic's sovereignty.

title: Treaty of Friendship with Italy
description: San Marino signed a treaty of friendship and cooperation with the newly unified Kingdom of Italy.

title: San Marino Joins the United Nations
description: San Marino became a member of the United Nations, gaining a presence in international diplomacy.

title: Monte Titano Named World Heritage Site
description: UNESCO inscribed San Marino's historic centre and Monte Titano on the World Heritage List.

title: Kingdom of Serbia Established
description: Stefan Nemanjić was crowned king, founding the medieval Serbian kingdom under the Nemanjić dynasty.

title: Serbian Orthodox Church Autocephaly
description: Saint Sava secured autocephaly for the Serbian Orthodox Church, becoming its first archbishop.

title: Battle of Kosovo
description: Serbian forces fought the Ottoman Empire at Kosovo, a defining event in Serbian national memory.

title: First Serbian Uprising
description: Led by Karađorđe, Serbs rose against Ottoman rule, beginning the path toward modern Serbian statehood.

title: Serbia Gains Independence
description: The Congress of Berlin recognized Serbia as a fully independent state from the Ottoman Empire.

title: Kingdom of Yugoslavia Formed
description: Serbia joined other South Slavs in the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia.

title: Serbia Becomes Independent
description: After Montenegro's referendum, the state union dissolved and Serbia became an independent republic.

title: Great Moravia Emerges
description: The Slavic state of Great Moravia rose, encompassing much of present-day Slovakia.

title: Mission of Cyril and Methodius
description: The brothers Cyril and Methodius brought Christianity and Slavic literacy to Great Moravia.

title: Universitas Istropolitana Founded
description: The first university on Slovak territory was established in Bratislava (Pressburg) by Matthias Corvinus.

title: Czechoslovakia Founded
description: Slovaks joined Czechs to form the independent state of Czechoslovakia after World War I.

title: Slovak National Uprising
description: Slovak resistance forces rose against Nazi German occupation and the collaborationist regime.

title: Independent Slovakia Established
description: The peaceful 'Velvet Divorce' split Czechoslovakia, creating the sovereign Slovak Republic.

title: Slovakia Joins the EU and NATO
description: Slovakia became a member of both the European Union and NATO, anchoring it in Western institutions.

title: Slovakia Adopts the Euro
description: Slovakia joined the eurozone, replacing the koruna with the euro currency.

title: Principality of Carantania
description: Carantania, an early Slavic principality, emerged in the region encompassing modern Slovenia.

title: First Books in Slovene
description: Primož Trubar published the first printed books in Slovene, founding the Slovene literary language.

title: Joins Kingdom of Yugoslavia
description: Slovenia joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes after the collapse of Austria-Hungary.

title: Slovenia Declares Independence
description: Slovenia declared independence from Yugoslavia, followed by the brief Ten-Day War.

title: International Recognition
description: Slovenia gained widespread international recognition and joined the United Nations as a sovereign state.

title: Slovenia Joins the EU and NATO
description: Slovenia became a member of the European Union and NATO, integrating with Western Europe.

title: Slovenia Adopts the Euro
description: Slovenia became the first former Yugoslav state to join the eurozone, adopting the euro.

title: Phoenicians Found Cádiz
description: Phoenician traders established Gadir (Cádiz), one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Western Europe.

title: Roman Conquest of Hispania Begins
description: Rome began its conquest of the Iberian Peninsula during the Second Punic War, founding Hispania.

title: Umayyad Conquest of Hispania
description: Muslim forces crossed from North Africa and conquered most of the Iberian Peninsula, founding Al-Andalus.

title: Granada Falls and Columbus Sails
description: The Catholic Monarchs completed the Reconquista and sponsored Columbus's voyage to the Americas.

title: Habsburg Spain Unified
description: Charles I became king, uniting the Spanish crowns and launching a vast global empire.

title: Spanish Civil War Begins
description: A military uprising sparked a civil war that led to the dictatorship of Francisco Franco.

title: Democratic Constitution Adopted
description: Spain adopted a democratic constitution after Franco's death, establishing a parliamentary monarchy.

title: Spain Joins the EEC
description: Spain became a member of the European Economic Community, consolidating its return to democratic Europe.

title: Kalmar Union Formed
description: Sweden joined Denmark and Norway under one monarch in the Kalmar Union.

title: Gustav Vasa Becomes King
description: Gustav Vasa led Sweden out of the Kalmar Union and was crowned king, founding the modern Swedish state.

title: Reign of Gustavus Adolphus
description: Gustavus Adolphus began his reign, turning Sweden into a leading European military power.

title: End of the Great Northern War
description: The Treaty of Nystad ended the Great Northern War, marking the decline of the Swedish Empire.

title: Sweden's Last War
description: Sweden entered a long period of peace and neutrality after a brief war with Norway, unbroken since.

title: First Nobel Prizes Awarded
description: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in Stockholm under the will of Alfred Nobel.

title: Sweden Joins the European Union
description: Sweden became a member of the European Union following a national referendum.

title: Founding of the Swiss Confederation
description: The cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden formed a pact, traditionally seen as the origin of Switzerland.

title: Swabian War Won
description: The Swiss Confederation gained de facto independence from the Holy Roman Empire after the Swabian War.

title: Formal Independence Recognized
description: The Peace of Westphalia formally recognized Swiss independence from the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Swiss Neutrality Guaranteed
description: The Congress of Vienna recognized Switzerland's perpetual neutrality and confirmed its borders.

title: Federal Constitution Adopted
description: Switzerland adopted a federal constitution, creating the modern federal state and central government.

title: Red Cross Founded in Geneva
description: Henry Dunant helped found the International Committee of the Red Cross in Geneva.

title: Women Gain the Vote Nationally
description: Swiss women won the right to vote in federal elections following a national referendum.

title: Switzerland Joins the United Nations
description: Switzerland became a full member of the United Nations after a national referendum.

title: Kievan Rus Centered on Kyiv
description: Oleg established Kyiv as the center of Kievan Rus, a foundational state in Ukrainian history.

title: Baptism of Kievan Rus
description: Vladimir the Great adopted Orthodox Christianity in Kyiv, shaping the region's religious culture.

title: Khmelnytsky Uprising
description: Bohdan Khmelnytsky led a Cossack uprising that created the Cossack Hetmanate, a Ukrainian state.

title: Holodomor Famine
description: A man-made famine under Soviet policy killed millions of Ukrainians, remembered as a national tragedy.

title: Chernobyl Disaster
description: A reactor explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear plant caused history's worst nuclear accident.

title: Ukraine Declares Independence
description: Ukraine declared independence from the Soviet Union, confirmed by an overwhelming referendum.

title: Orange Revolution
description: Mass protests over a disputed election led to a rerun and a peaceful transfer of power.

title: Revolution of Dignity
description: The Euromaidan protests ousted the president and reoriented Ukraine toward closer ties with Europe.

title: Roman Conquest of Britain
description: Emperor Claudius launched the Roman conquest of Britain in AD 43, founding the province of Britannia.

title: Norman Conquest of England
description: William the Conqueror defeated King Harold at the Battle of Hastings, transforming English society.

title: Magna Carta Sealed
description: King John sealed Magna Carta, limiting royal power and influencing later constitutional law.

title: Acts of Union Create Great Britain
description: England and Scotland united to form the Kingdom of Great Britain under a single parliament.

title: Industrial Revolution Begins
description: Around this time Britain pioneered the Industrial Revolution, transforming manufacturing and society.

title: Victorian Era Begins
description: Queen Victoria's reign began a period of imperial expansion, industry, and global influence.

title: Founding Member of the UN
description: The United Kingdom became a founding member of the United Nations after World War II.

title: United Kingdom Leaves the EU
description: The UK formally left the European Union following the 2016 Brexit referendum.

title: Traditional Martyrdom of Saint Peter
description: Saint Peter is traditionally believed to have been martyred in Rome, where St. Peter's Basilica now stands.

title: Old St. Peter's Basilica Begun
description: Emperor Constantine began constructing the original basilica over the tomb of Saint Peter.

title: Papal States Established
description: The Donation of Pepin granted territories to the Pope, founding the Papal States in central Italy.

title: New St. Peter's Basilica Begun
description: Pope Julius II laid the foundation for the present St. Peter's Basilica, a masterpiece of Renaissance art.

title: End of the Papal States
description: The Kingdom of Italy annexed Rome, ending the temporal rule of the Papal States.

title: Vatican City Founded
description: The Lateran Treaty between the Holy See and Italy created the independent state of Vatican City.

title: Second Vatican Council Opens
description: Pope John XXIII convened the Second Vatican Council, leading to major reforms in the Catholic Church.
